slice: Browser rendering of Gaussian splats and splat file formats, mid-2026 state — Spark, PlayCanvas SuperSplat/SOG, mkkellogg GaussianSplats3D, Babylon.js, splat-transform, camera-path authoring
summary: The mid-2026 web-splat stack has consolidated hard around PlayCanvas's tooling and Spark's renderer, with the old antimatter15-lineage (.splat, mkkellogg/GaussianSplats3D) explicitly deprecated by its own maintainer in favor of Spark. Format-wise, PlayCanvas's SOG (Spatially-Ordered Gaussians, announced Sept 2025, "the WebP of Gaussian Splatting") has become the de facto browser-delivery format: WebP-textured, Morton-ordered, GPU-decode-ready, cutting a 1GB PLY to 42MB. It's natively supported by Spark (since late 2025) and Babylon.js v9 (March 26, 2026), and is produced by PlayCanvas's open-source splat-transform CLI, which now reads/writes PLY, SOG, Streamed SOG, SPZ, SPLAT, KSPLAT, GLB, and even bakes voxel-collision octrees and standalone HTML viewers. Niantic Spatial's SPZ format shipped v4 (May 5, 2026) with 3-5x faster encoding, an uncapped point count, and SH degree-4 support, and sits at the center of Khronos's new KHR_gaussian_splatting glTF extension (release-candidate Feb 3, 2026, ratification expected Q2 2026) — making SPZ the better long-term interchange bet even though SOG currently wins for raw in-browser decode. Spark (sparkjs.dev, MIT, World Labs) shipped a major v2.0 (April 2026) LOD "splat tree" for 100M+ splat worlds and v2.1 (May 2026), remains WebGL2-only, and has no built-in keyframe timeline — that job now belongs to PlayCanvas SuperSplat, whose Timeline panel (v2.0, Feb 2025) can auto-seed camera keyframes from COLMAP poses and, as of v2.2, renders fly-through MP4s locally in-browser with zero upload. Babylon.js v9 added splat shadows, native SOG loading, and experimental sort-free "Triangle Splatting."

sources.title: New Features in 2.0 - Spark
key_claims: Spark 2.0 introduces a Level-of-Detail (LoD) Splat Tree traversed in O(N log N) time for steady frame rate on huge scenes
Handles scenes with 100M or 1G+ splats via a default 16M-splat GPU memory pool
Adds a .RAD streamable LoD format for HTTP Range-request loading and a SparkXr WebXR wrapper with hand tracking
quotes: can traverse the tree in O(N log N) time

sources.title: Releases · sparkjsdev/spark
key_claims: v2.1.0 released May 18, 2026 with PLY point-cloud enhancements and a Chrome 149 compatibility fix
v2.0.0 released April 14, 2026 introducing the LOD system
v0.1.10 (Oct 25, 2025) added SOGSv2 compression support; v0.1.9 (Sep 22, 2025) added SPZ v3 compatibility

sources.title: PlayCanvas Open Sources SOG: The WebP of Gaussian Splatting
key_claims: SOG stores splat data as WebP images in Morton order for GPU-ready decoding without post-load processing
A showcase scene compresses 1GB of PLY data (4M gaussians) down to 42MB, a ~95% reduction, roughly 2-3x better than compressed PLY
Engine support landed in PlayCanvas Engine 2.11.0; spec and reference implementation are open-sourced

sources.title: splat-transform README
key_claims: Reads PLY, Compressed PLY, SOG, Streamed SOG, SPZ, SPLAT, KSPLAT, LCC, LCC2; writes PLY, Compressed PLY, SOG, Streamed SOG, SPZ, GLB, CSV, HTML Viewer, LOD, Voxel, WebP
Supports Morton reordering, NaN/Inf stripping, box/sphere/harmonic-band/floater filters, and sparse voxel octree generation for collision
Installable via npm as @playcanvas/splat-transform, or usable browser-side via WebAssembly at superspl.at/convert

sources.title: SPZ 4 is here: leaner, faster, and more future-proof
key_claims: SPZ 4 compresses ~3-5x faster and loads ~1.5-2.1x faster than SPZ3, e.g. 1min8s vs 3min26s encoding a 34M-point dataset
Replaces the single GZip stream with six parallel ZSTD streams for multi-core compression, removes the old 10M-point cap, and raises SH support to degree 4 with configurable 3/5/8-bit quantization
Files remain roughly 10x smaller than uncompressed PLY
quotes: SPZ 4 compresses about 3-5x faster, loads roughly 1.5-2x faster end-to-end

sources.title: GaussianSplats3D (mkkellogg) — GitHub repository
key_claims: Latest tagged release is v0.4.7 (Jan 25, 2025), adding PlayCanvas export and SPZ compression support
Supports .ply, .splat, and .ksplat formats with built-in orbit camera controls
README states the project is no longer in active development and directs users to Spark instead
quotes: this repo is no longer in active development

sources.title: Babylon.js V9.0: 3DGS Gets Shadows, SOGs, and Triangle Splatting Support Announced
key_claims: Babylon.js v9.0 (March 26, 2026) adds shadow-casting for Gaussian splat meshes and native loading of the SOG/SOGS format from Fraunhofer HHI
Adds experimental 'Triangle Splatting' (Univ. of Liège/UCLouvain technique) replacing gaussian ellipsoids with opaque triangles for sort-free depth-correct rendering
Unifies loading of .splat, .ply, .spz, and .sog through one pipeline; adds orthographic-camera support for splats

sources.title: SuperSplat 2.0 lets you create flythroughs of 3D Gaussian Splats
key_claims: SuperSplat 2.0's Timeline panel lets users set per-frame camera keyframes to build smooth flythrough animations
SuperSplat can import COLMAP camera poses to auto-generate timeline keyframes recreating the original scan path

sources.title: Render Your Gaussian Splats to Video with SuperSplat 2.2
key_claims: SuperSplat's Render menu exports high-quality video directly from Timeline camera animations, with resolution/bitrate controls and vertical-video export
Rendering happens entirely locally in-browser; no splat or render data is uploaded to any server

sources.title: Khronos Announces glTF Gaussian Splatting Extension (press release)
key_claims: KHR_gaussian_splatting release candidate announced Feb 3, 2026 for glTF 2.0, extending mesh primitives with per-gaussian position, orientation, scale, color and opacity
Ratification expected Q2 2026; contributors include Autodesk, Bentley Systems/Cesium, Esri, Huawei, Niantic Spatial, NVIDIA, and XGRIDS
Design allows graceful fallback to point-cloud rendering in viewers lacking splat support
quotes: helping ensure this powerful new rendering technique can scale across tools, platforms, and the web

sources.title: nianticlabs/spz — GitHub repository (license)
key_claims: SPZ file format library is dual-licensed Apache-2.0 OR MIT
Originally open-sourced by Niantic in late 2024 as a ~10x-smaller-than-PLY compressed splat format

sources.title: SparkRenderer docs - Spark
key_claims: SparkRenderer requires a THREE.WebGLRenderer (WebGL2) instance and disables antialiasing since it doesn't help splat rendering; no WebGPU path documented
Offers radial vs Z-depth splat sorting and configurable target splat counts: ~500K-750K for WebXR, 1-1.5M mobile, 2.5M desktop via lodSplatScale

recommendations: Standardize the shipped web-viewer artifact on PlayCanvas's .sog (Spatially-Ordered Gaussians) format instead of the current ad-hoc 'artifact.splat' — SOG is Morton-ordered WebP-backed data that decodes GPU-ready with no per-splat CPU unpack, is natively supported by Spark (since v0.1.6, SOGSv2 since v0.1.10) and Babylon.js v9, and PlayCanvas's own showcase shrinks a 1GB PLY to 42MB (~95% smaller) at 4M gaussians — 2-3x better than compressed PLY.

Keep .ply (or compressed .ply) as the archival/master format straight out of gsplat/Brush training, and insert one conversion step using the open-source @playcanvas/splat-transform CLI (Node) to filter NaN/floaters, Morton-reorder, and emit both the archive PLY and a Streamed SOG (auto-LOD'd if the bridge+roadway scene exceeds 1M gaussians) for the web bundle. This replaces any hand-rolled format-writing code.

Do not add WebGPU or switch renderers: Spark (sparkjs.dev, MIT, backed by World Labs) is WebGL2-only but actively developed (v2.1.0 May 18 2026, v2.0.0 April 14 2026 added an LOD splat tree for 100M-1B+ splat scenes), and is exactly what mkkellogg explicitly tells GaussianSplats3D users to migrate to since his repo 'is no longer in active development' (last release v0.4.7, Jan 2025). Orbit Studio's existing Spark/three.js viewer choice is already the right one — just feed it .sog instead of raw .splat.

For keyframed fly-through camera paths, do not build a custom timeline UI in Orbit Studio's own viewer. Instead route trained scenes through the free, open-source SuperSplat editor (superspl.at/editor): its Timeline panel can import the COLMAP camera poses Orbit Studio already computes via pycolmap to auto-seed keyframes matching the real capture path, then let the user hand-adjust and use SuperSplat 2.2's local, no-upload Render menu to export an MP4 fly-through directly in-browser.

For the interactive (non-video) fly-through experience, export the SuperSplat-authored keyframe/path data and drive it through a thin custom THREE.Camera interpolator inside the existing Spark viewer — Spark is explicitly camera-control-agnostic ('any camera control scheme compatible with THREE.js'), so this is a small integration, not a new subsystem.

Add Niantic's SPZ (Apache-2.0 OR MIT, github.com/nianticlabs/spz) only as a secondary/interchange export — not the primary web format — for users who want to pull the bridge scene into other engines (Unity, robotics, etc.); SPZ 4 (May 5 2026) is 3-5x faster to encode and now uncaps the old 10M-point limit, and it's the format named in Khronos's KHR_gaussian_splatting glTF extension (release candidate Feb 3, 2026) contributor list, so it's the better long-term portability bet even though SOG currently wins for raw browser decode speed.

Flag to the user that KHR_gaussian_splatting (glTF 2.0 Gaussian-splat extension, backed by Autodesk/Bentley-Cesium/Esri/Huawei/Niantic Spatial/NVIDIA) is still pre-ratification as of this research (release candidate Feb 2026, ratification 'expected Q2 2026' — actual ratification date unconfirmed) — worth revisiting in a few months but not yet something to build against.
uncertainties: Whether KHR_gaussian_splatting has actually been ratified by Khronos as of today (July 23, 2026) — only a Feb 3, 2026 release-candidate announcement with ratification 'expected Q2 2026' was confirmed; no ratification-complete announcement was found.
Whether Spark has shipped any release beyond v2.1.0 (May 18, 2026) between then and July 23, 2026 — the releases page fetch may not reflect the very latest tag.
Whether Spark has added or roadmapped WebGPU support — current docs describe a WebGL2-only renderer with no WebGPU path mentioned either way.
Exact mechanism SuperSplat 2.2 uses for local video export (e.g., WebCodecs vs MediaRecorder) was not confirmed from source text.
Whether Babylon.js's native SOG loader and Spark's SOG loader are cross-compatible with the exact same .sog files (both claim SOG/SOGS support but interop wasn't independently verified).
Whether splat-transform's 'HTML Viewer' export target uses Spark, PlayCanvas engine, or another renderer under the hood — not stated in the fetched README excerpt.
